channel.title: Writings — Suraj Sharma, XO Labs
channel.description: Long-form research on agentic systems and the measurement of work.

item.title: XO Space: the architecture
item.description: The implementation reference for xo-space: install and run, the xo-project folder contract, and the full data model — every entity collected, what bounds each file, and where the plane duplicates itself.

item.title: The J-Space: a construction manual
item.description: What the Jacobian Lens is, why averaging is the whole trick, and exactly how to build a J-space — compute routes, sparse decomposition, read and write operations, and a validation protocol.

item.title: One Graph, No Boxes
item.description: A close reading of Click and Paleczny's 1995 paper, the origin of the Sea of Nodes — every figure redrawn — and the general recipe inside it for representing any process over any data.

item.title: The Sea of Nodes, explained simply
item.description: A plain-language explanation of the program representation behind V8's TurboFan: three kinds of edges, why pure instructions float, how the graph becomes a program again, and why V8 left it.

item.title: Anatomy of an Agent Control Plane
item.description: A teardown of xo-space, the local control plane for AI coding agents: one capability seam, agents declared as data, four transports under one streaming contract, and a session index that holds no messages.

item.title: Anatomy of a Personal Memory Engine
item.description: A component-by-component teardown of iai-pme, a fully local memory engine for coding agents: fail-safe capture hooks, an encrypted verbatim store, a vector index that isn't HNSW, and nightly consolidation.

item.title: What is a unit of work?
item.description: A prompt asks for an action. A unit of work owns an outcome from definition through verification. The quirq is the proposed unit for measuring that verified work.

item.title: quirq: A Unit of Work for Intelligence
item.description: The token meters what AI consumes. The quirq is proposed as the output meter: budgeted by an owner, minted by verification, costed all-in, read as a trajectory.
